module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt: After you save the record, select the **Service agreement** tab from the Action Pane. Go to **Relations > Service objects** or **Service tasks** to create a new service object or service tasks for the service agreement. By expanding the **Lines** FastTab, you can create service agreement lines. You can copy lines from a service template, another service agreement, or you can create them manually.

This directly supports the claim.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: A service agreement can be created from the Project module in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
## Create a service agreement from Project

To create a service agreement from Project, go to **Project management and accounting > Projects > All projects**. Select a project from the list. On the **Projects** page, select **Manage** on the Action Pane and then select **New > Service > Service agreement**. Select **New** on the Action Pane and then enter the necessary information to create a service agreement. Select **Save** to save the service agreement.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn directly confirms this. The current "Create service agreements" documentation has a section titled "Create a service agreement from Project" with steps: go to **Project management and accounting > All projects**, select a project, then **Manage > New > Service > Service agreement**.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: Service intervals in service agreements define the scheduled frequency for performing services or generating service orders for a customer.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
In Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, service intervals in service agreements refer to the scheduled frequency at which you perform services or generate service orders for a customer. These intervals are part of the service agreement and help automate the creation of service orders over time.

To create a service interval, go to **Service management > Setup > Service agreements > Service intervals**. Select **New** on the Action Pane. Enter an ID in the **Service interval** field and a **Description**. Select a range in the **Range** field and then specify the **Frequency**. Select **Save** when you’re done.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation confirms that a service agreement interval indicates the frequency with which service order lines are created for service agreement lines when service orders are created automatically, and that service orders are created according to that interval from the agreement line start date. This supports the claim’s main point that service intervals define the scheduled frequency for recurring service activity/service order generation.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: Creating planned service orders from a service agreement and its lines can generate service orders and service order lines for a future period.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt: After you create a service agreement and service agreement lines, you can create planned service orders and service order lines for the coming months. On the **Service agreements** page, select **Deliver** on the Action Pane and then select **Create > Planned service orders**. On the **Create service orders** page, enter the current date in the **From** field. In the **To date** field, enter a date one month from now. Set **Hour** to **Yes** and then select **OK**.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management confirms this workflow. The official page says you can select a service agreement, use **Deliver > Planned service orders**, specify **From date** and **To date** to define the service period, and that selected transaction types from service agreement lines generate several service orders depending on the service interval. Related docs also state service orders are generated based on a service agreement for the valid period of the agreement.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: Time windows control how far a service order line can be moved from its scheduled date.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
Time windows indicate the allowable range for a service order line to deviate from its scheduled date. The system determines this scheduled date by the interval settings and the service period that you specify on the **Create service orders** page. The following values are available for defining a time window:

- **Week** – You can reschedule the service order line to any available day within the same week as the originally calculated date.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management states that "Time windows specify how far a service order line can move from its calculated date," and also says the time window defines how far a service order line can move relative to its calculated date. That directly supports the claim.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: If a time window uses the Manual method, you must specify how many days before or after the calculated date the system can move the service order line.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
## Create time windows 

To create a time window, go to **Service management > Setup > Service agreements > Time window**. Select **New** on the Action Pane to create a new time window. Enter a name in the **Time window** field and a description in the **Description** field. Select a **Method** for automatic creation.

> [!NOTE]
> If you select **Manual**, then you need to specify the number of days before or after the calculated date that the system can move the service order line. This flexibility can help your organization manage scheduling and resource allocation effectively.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management explicitly states: "If the method is of the Manual type, specify the number of days before or after the calculated date that the service order line can be moved." The related Time windows page also says Manual means you define the maximum number of days before or after the initial calculated date that the service order line can be moved.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: Service tasks can be linked to a specific service agreement or service order by creating service task relations.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
Your organization can use service tasks to outline the tasks that need to be completed during a service order. This information is accessible to technicians and customers. You can create service tasks on the **Service tasks** page and then link them to a specific service agreement or service order by establishing service task relations.

After you establish a service task relation between a service task and a service order or service agreement, you can select this service task when creating service order lines or service agreement lines for the relevant service order or agreement.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation explicitly confirms this. The current "Service tasks overview" page states that you associate service tasks with a specific service agreement or service order by creating service task relations, and the "Create service task relations" page provides steps for creating those relations for both service agreements and service orders.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: When generating service orders from a service agreement, service tasks associated with each service agreement line can be used to consolidate service order lines into organized service orders.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
After you establish a service task relation between a service task and a service order or service agreement, you can select this service task when creating service order lines or service agreement lines for the relevant service order or agreement. When generating service orders from a service agreement, you can use the service tasks that are associated with each service agreement line to consolidate service order lines into organized service orders.

## Create a service task
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.reasoning: Microsoft Learn’s current Service tasks documentation explicitly states: “When you generate service orders from a service agreement, you can use the service tasks that are assigned to each service agreement line to group service order lines into service orders.” It also documents selecting **By service task** in the **Combine service orders** field to group service orders by service task ID.

module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.claim: To have the system group automatically generated service orders by service task, the service agreement's Combine service orders field must be set to By service task.
module-10bbd62085690d38ef81c790b3565c4d0.excerpt:
## Group service orders

When you want to have the system automatically create service orders, you can use service tasks as a basis for grouping. To group service orders by service tasks, you need to specify in the service agreement that the system should initially group service orders that it generates from service tasks by service task ID. Lakeflow Jobs supports several trigger types that determine when your jobs run. While scheduled triggers run at fixed times, event-based triggers respond to data changes in your environment.

| Trigger type | Behavior |
|--------------|----------|
| **Table update** | Runs when monitored tables receive new data or modifications |
| **File arrival** | Runs when new files appear in a Unity Catalog storage location |
| **Continuous** | Runs immediately after the previous run completes or fails |

## Understand notification events

Azure Databricks can notify you when specific events occur during job execution. Each event type serves a different operational purpose.

| Event type            | When it fires                            | Use case                                                 |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Start**             | Job run begins                           | Track job initiation, confirm scheduled jobs started     |
| **Success**           | Job completes successfully               | Verify pipeline completion, trigger downstream processes |
| **Failure**           | Job terminates with error                | Investigate issues, initiate incident response           |
| **Duration warning**  | Run exceeds configured threshold         | Identify performance degradation, catch runaway jobs     |
| **Streaming backlog** | Backlog exceeds threshold for 10 minutes | Monitor streaming job health                             |

However, Windows PowerShell can and does apply application-level encryption by default. This means that your communications receive a degree of privacy and protection. On internal networks, this application-level encryption is generally sufficient to satisfy organizational security requirements.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation supports this. Current PowerShell remoting guidance says WinRM listens on HTTP 5985 and HTTPS 5986, and the training path itself says the default configuration uses HTTP on port 5985. The current security documentation also states that regardless of HTTP or HTTPS, WinRM encrypts all PowerShell remoting communication after initial authentication; over HTTP it uses message-level encryption negotiated by the authentication protocol.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: When using HTTP with Basic authentication to a computer not configured for HTTPS, credentials including passwords are transmitted in clear text.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: When you connect by using HTTPS, the entire channel is encrypted by using the encryption keys of the remote computer’s SSL certificate. As a result, even if you use Basic authentication, passwords are not transmitted in clear text. However, when you connect by using HTTP and Basic authentication to a computer that isn't configured for HTTPS, credentials (including passwords) will be transmitted in clear text.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation for WinRM/PowerShell remoting confirms this. The current WinRM configuration docs state that Basic authentication is a scheme in which the user name and password are sent in clear text, and the PowerShell remoting security guidance says Basic authentication provides no encryption for HTTP connections. That directly supports the claim.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Only computers that receive incoming PowerShell remoting connections need remoting enabled; outgoing connections do not require remoting configuration beyond allowing outbound traffic.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt:
It's important to understand that you need to enable Windows PowerShell remoting only on computers that will receive incoming connections. No configuration is necessary to enable outgoing communications, except for making sure that any local firewall will allow the outgoing traffic.

## Manually enabling PowerShell remoting

PowerShell remoting is enabled by default on Windows Server platforms.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn currently states that supported Windows computers can establish remote PowerShell connections without any configuration, but to receive remote connections you must enable PowerShell remoting. The Enable-PSRemoting documentation also says you only need to run it on computers that receive commands, not on computers that only send them. This supports the claim’s main point. The docs also confirm PowerShell remoting is enabled by default on Windows Server 2012 and newer.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Enabling PowerShell remoting manually requires local Administrator privileges.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: PowerShell remoting is enabled by default on Windows Server platforms. You can enable PowerShell remoting on other supported Windows versions, and you can also re-enable remoting if it becomes disabled. To manually enable Windows PowerShell remoting on a computer, run the Windows PowerShell Enable-PSRemoting cmdlet. This is a persistent change that you can disable later by running Disable-PSRemoting. Note that this task requires the privileges granted to local Administrators group.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation for about_Remote_Requirements says to configure a computer to receive remote commands you should start PowerShell with the **Run as administrator** option and then run `Enable-PSRemoting`. The same page also states that administrator privileges are required for remoting operations involving local WS-Management settings and session configurations, which `Enable-PSRemoting` changes. This supports the claim.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Enable-PSRemoting starts the WinRM service, sets it to Automatic, creates a listener on any IP address, enables a WS-Management firewall exception, creates session endpoint configurations if needed, enables all session configurations, and updates their security descriptors for remote access.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt:
The Enable-PSRemoting cmdlet performs the following operations:
1. Runs the Set-WSManQuickConfig cmdlet, which in turn performs the following tasks:
- Starts the WinRM service.
- Sets the startup type on the WinRM service to Automatic.
- Creates a listener to accept requests on any IP address.
- Enables a firewall exception for WS-Management communications.
- Creates the simple-name and long-name session endpoint configurations, if needed.
- Enables all session configurations.
- Changes the security descriptor of all session configurations to allow remote access.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Current Microsoft Learn documentation for Enable-PSRemoting explicitly lists these operations: it runs Set-WSManQuickConfig, which starts WinRM, sets it to Automatic, creates a listener on any IP address, enables a WS-Management firewall exception, creates simple and long-name session endpoint configurations if needed, enables all session configurations, and changes their security descriptors to allow remote access.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Invoke-Command adds a PSComputerName property to returned objects so you can identify which computer each result came from.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: One-to-many remoting lets you send a single command to multiple computers in parallel. Each computer will run the command that you transmit, serialize the results into XML, and transmit those results back to your computer. Your computer then deserializes the XML into objects and puts them into the Windows PowerShell pipeline. When doing this, several properties are added to each object, including a PSComputerName property that indicates which computer each result came from.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation for Invoke-Command shows output with a PSComputerName column and explicitly states that the output includes the PsComputerName property containing the name of the computer on which the command ran. The PowerShell remoting learning content on Microsoft Learn also shows one-to-many remoting output with a PSComputerName column.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: By default, Windows PowerShell connects to only 32 computers at once for a command, and additional connections are queued.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: To help you manage the resources on your local computer, PowerShell includes a per-command throttling feature that lets you limit the number of concurrent remote connections established for each command. By default, Windows PowerShell will connect to only 32 computers at once. If you list more than 32 computers, the connections to the other computers will be queued. Once sessions to some of the computers from the first batch complete and return their results, connections to the computers in the next batch will be initiated.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn's current PowerShell Remoting FAQ says remoting uses a per-command throttling feature and that the default is 32 concurrent remote connections. While the current FAQ doesn't explicitly use the word "queued," that behavior is consistent with the documented throttle limit for additional targets beyond the concurrent cap. The claim's main guidance is still correct.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: The -ThrottleLimit parameter on Invoke-Command changes the number of concurrent remote connections and increases load on the local computer rather than the remote computers.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: You can alter this behavior by using the –ThrottleLimit parameter of Invoke-Command. Raising the number doesn't put an extra load on the remote computers. However, it does put an extra load on the computer where Invoke-Command was invoked. It also utilizes more bandwidth.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn's PowerShell Remoting FAQ says throttling "lets you limit the number of concurrent remote connections" for each command and that it exists "to help you manage the resources on your local computer." That supports the claim's main point: -ThrottleLimit controls concurrent remote connections and is primarily about local resource usage rather than remote-computer load.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Variables defined locally are not available inside a remote script block unless passed in explicitly.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt:
The script block or file contents are transmitted as literal text to the remote computers that run them exactly as is. The computer doesn't parse the script block or file on which the Invoke-Command was run. Consider the following command example:

$var = 'BITS'
Invoke-Command –ScriptBlock { Get-Service –Name $var } –Computer LON-DC1

In this scenario, the variable $var is being set on the local computer rather than being included into the script block to be run on LON-DC1. In other words, $var is not defined or set in the PowerShell remoting session to LON-DC1.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn's current PowerShell docs state that, by default, variables used in remote commands are assumed to be defined in the remote session. Local variables must be explicitly passed into the remote script block, such as with the `Using:` scope modifier or `Invoke-Command -ArgumentList`. That directly supports the claim.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Each Invoke-Command call creates a new wsmprovhost process on the remote computer, so state such as variables does not persist across separate calls.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: Using the techniques outlined here, every time you use Invoke-Command, the remote computer creates a new wsmprovhost process, and runs the command or commands. It then returns the results, and then closes that Windows PowerShell instance. Each successive Invoke-Command, even if made to the same computer, is akin to opening a new Windows PowerShell window. Any work done by a previous session won't exist unless you save it to a disk or some other persistent storage.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation clearly supports the persistence part of this claim: when you use Invoke-Command with the ComputerName parameter, PowerShell creates a temporary connection, closes it when the command completes, and any variables or functions defined in that temporary session are lost. Learn also contrasts this with using New-PSSession and Invoke-Command -Session for persistent state across commands. I did not find current Learn documentation explicitly stating the specific remote process name wsmprovhost, but the claim’s substantive guidance about non-persistent state across separate Invoke-Command calls is confirmed.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: New-PSSession creates persistent sessions that can be reused across multiple Invoke-Command calls.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: For more interactive Windows PowerShell remoting situations, you can manage individual sessions as separate entities. To do this, you first create a session by using the New-PSSession command. The benefit of using the New-PSSession command is that the session will persist throughout multiple Invoke-Command instances, allowing you to pass variables and objects to other commands in your script.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation explicitly supports this. The about_PSSession_Details page states that when you use New-PSSession, PowerShell establishes a persistent session that remains open for multiple commands. The Invoke-Command documentation also says to use New-PSSession to create a PSSession and then use Invoke-Command -Session to run a series of related commands that share data, with an example showing the same session reused across multiple Invoke-Command calls.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Objects returned from remote commands are deserialized objects without methods or events.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt: When your computer receives the XML, it's deserialized back into objects that are put in the Windows PowerShell pipeline. When you have a Process object, by piping it to Get-Member, you know it's now of the type Deserialized.System.Diagnostics.Process, a related, but different, kind of object. The deserialized object has no methods and no events.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation on `about_Remote_Output` and the PowerShell Remoting FAQ says output from remote commands is serialized and returned to the local computer as deserialized objects. It explicitly states these deserialized objects are snapshots, not live objects, and that they include properties but no methods. That clearly supports the claim’s main point about remote output being deserialized and lacking live object behavior.

module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.claim: Actions that must interact with remote objects should be performed inside the remote script block, not on deserialized objects returned to the local computer.
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.excerpt:
Given the serialization and deserialization which is part of PowerShell remoting, you should consider any objects that are obtained in this manner to be a static snapshot. The values of object properties are not updatable, and the objects cannot be used to perform any actions. Therefore, any tasks that require interacting with remote objects should be performed on the remote computer as part of the PowerShell remoting session.

For example, here is an example of a command that will not yield the desired results:

Invoke-Command –Computer LON-DC1 –ScriptBlock { Get-Process –Name Note* } |
Stop-Process
module-84686a756186b554ab685309ee5a1944d.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation supports this directly. The PowerShell remoting docs state that results returned by Invoke-Command are deserialized objects—'inert snapshots' with most methods missing—and explicitly say you can't act on those returned objects locally; instead, 'you must call the method within the remote session.' The Stop-Process docs also note that stopping a process on a remote computer should be done with Invoke-Command on the remote machine.

module-ae4f08c593156cffd4af283ca4134c375.claim: An Azure resource deployed to a virtual network receives a private IP address from the virtual network range.
module-ae4f08c593156cffd4af283ca4134c375.excerpt:
Virtual networks are isolated networking segments where you can deploy workloads so they're only accessible privately, or optionally also over the public internet. Virtual networks typically host VMs, but you can also deploy other Azure resources like container instances to virtual networks.

An Azure resource deployed to a virtual network receives a private IP address from the virtual network range. The private IP is reachable only from inside the virtual network, from peered virtual networks, or from on-premises networks connected via Site-to-Site VPN or Azure ExpressRoute.

Azure Container Apps implements and manages revisions as follows:

- You can create new revisions by updating a previous revision.
- You can retain up to 100 revisions, giving you a historical record of your container app updates.
- You can run multiple revisions concurrently.
- You can split external HTTP traffic between active revisions.

This supports the claim’s main point that Azure Container Apps lets you retain up to 100 revisions.

## Continuous deployment to Azure Container Apps

Azure Container Apps provides support for continuous deployment using either GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines. The scenarios below describe continuous deployments to a container app connected to container registry. Although the tools are distinct, they implement a similar process.

### Continuous deployment using GitHub Actions

module-09fcfa60730cc5798c1aa4c213b09cb43.claim: Microsoft-hosted agents in Azure Pipelines provide a fresh virtual machine for each job, and that virtual machine is discarded after the job completes.
module-09fcfa60730cc5798c1aa4c213b09cb43.excerpt:
If your pipelines are in Azure Pipelines, then you've got a convenient option to run your jobs using a Microsoft-hosted agent. With Microsoft-hosted agents, maintenance and upgrades are taken care of for you. Each time you run a pipeline, you get a fresh virtual machine for each job in the pipeline. The virtual machine is discarded after one job (which means any change that a job makes to the virtual machine file system, such as checking out code, will be unavailable to the next job). Microsoft-hosted agents can run jobs directly on the VM or in a container.

Azure Pipelines provides a predefined agent pool named Azure Pipelines with Microsoft-hosted agents.

## Kanban quantity calculation policies

In Supply Chain Management, a kanban quantity calculation policy is used
to define the parameters for the kanban quantity calculation and group
the kanban rules that are usually calculated in the same regularity with
the same parameters.

The kanban quantity calculation policy is then associated with the
kanban rules and used to perform the kanban calculation.

-   **Service level** - If **Include safety stock** is selected, a service
    level must be defined. For example, if the value of **90** is used, the
    fixed kanban quantity is calculated from an assumption that the

-   **Period** - Defines the period code for the calculation of demand.

module-8338601818e1028985a366af7deb666f6.excerpt:
## Calculating safety stock

In the general formula for calculating safety stock, it is assumed that
both lead time and material demands are not constant but vary over time
and that the variation of these sizes will follow a normal distribution.

Within Supply Chain Management, it is assumed that lead
time does not vary over time, thus the deviation over lead time will be
zero.

module-8338601818e1028985a366af7deb666f6.excerpt:
## Calculating average daily demand

The average daily demand for the periods in the kanban calculation is
calculated for both inventory-controlled and non-inventory controlled
kanban rules. These rules consider both fulfilled demand and future demand.

1. Go to Outbound marketing > Internet marketing > Marketing forms and then open an existing form. Go to the Summary tab and find the Content section. Make sure that the Prefill fields setting is set to Yes. (If this setting is set to No, then the form won't support prefilling for any fields).

Dynamic data masking limits sensitive data exposure by masking it to nonprivileged users. Dynamic data masking helps prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data by enabling customers to designate how much of the sensitive data to reveal with minimal effect on the application layer. It's a policy-based security feature that hides the sensitive data in the result set of a query over designated database fields, while the data in the database isn't changed.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: A production order can have the statuses Create, Estimate, Schedule, Release, Start, Report as finished, and End.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
The status on the production order reflects the sequential steps of the production life cycle. The following list is an overview of the status that a production order can have.

1. **Create** - The status of the production order when it is first created.
2. **Estimate** - The status of the production order after running a material and cost estimation.
3. **Schedule** - The status after running operation or job scheduling.
4. **Release** - The status when production orders are scheduled and have been released to production.
5. **Start** - The status of the production order when production starts.
6. **Report as finished** - The status of the production order when production is finished and ready for final action.
7. **End** - The status of the production order after final costs have been applied, the item is complete, and the order is no longer active.

Additional Learn content about reversing production order status also references the same sequence. The claim uses slightly shortened label forms, but the status progression is still supported.

## Product concept

A BOM consists of products that are in your inventory. Therefore, it's important to remind you about product definitions, which are created independently of a legal entity. Core values such as product number, type, and name are shared values across all legal entities in the organization. Some core values can be overridden by a legal entity, such as the search name, whereas other values are kept as key definition attributes and therefore cannot be changed other than on the product definition.

- **Item** - These types are products that are purchased or produced but are frequently included in the production of manufactured (BOM) items. - **Service** - These types are items that are used, such as the service that you're buying when you're sourcing an operation in a production order to a vendor, which is called subcontracting.

## Automatic estimation and scheduling

As a part of the production life-cycle steps, if a production is not already cost estimated or scheduled before it is ready to be released, Supply Chain Management can be set up to run the estimation and scheduling steps automatically.

Wait as long as you think it is practical before changing your orders with the status of **Scheduled** to the status of **Released**.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation supports this. The Production control parameters page includes an **Automatic update** tab that defines automatic updates as a production order moves through stages, and the training page states that "the system automatically updates the schedule when a production has been cost-estimated and released." It also documents that scheduling can auto-run estimation if an estimate hasn't already been done. Together, this confirms Supply Chain Management can be configured to run estimation and scheduling automatically.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: On the Release page, you can release a production that does not have Reported as finished or Cost accounted status.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
The fields on the **Overview** tab of the **Release** page are:

- **Production** - Specify the production number to be released. If you selected **Release** from the **Production orders** page, the fields are automatically filled in with the current production and the **Name** field is displayed. You can select any production that does not have the **Reported as finished** or **Cost accounted** status.
- **References** - If this check box is selected, references that are associated with the production are released under the same conditions that apply to this one.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Current Microsoft Learn documentation confirms that releasing a production order is part of the production lifecycle and that the release task is performed from a production order in Scheduled status. However, I couldn't find current official documentation that directly states the precise eligibility rule from the Release page as 'any production that does not have Reported as finished or Cost accounted status.' Because the available Learn pages don't explicitly verify or contradict that exact status filter, this claim is inconclusive.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
- **References** - If this check box is selected, references that are associated with the production are released under the same conditions that apply to this one. Only the current and any underlying productions are released.

**Cost management > Manufacturing accounting > Production orders > Process > Release**

To release all productions in the production hierarchy when you release the main production, indicate that the references must be released.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: Starting a production order changes its status to Started even if only part of the production is started.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
## Start production orders

When the production order is released, and reports are created, the next step is to start the production order. You can start all the operations in the production order, or only some, and save the rest until later. When the order is started, its status changes to **Started**, regardless of whether the complete production or only part of the production is started.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Microsoft Learn's current Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management documentation supports this. The production process overview says that once a production order is started, it is in the **Started** stage, and it also notes that production orders can be started in batches of the requested final quantity, meaning partial starts are supported while the order is still considered started.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: When a production order is started, the system by default suggests starting the quantity not yet started.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt: To start a production order, select **Production control > Production orders > All production orders**. Select the necessary production order and select **Start** from the Action Pane. When the production status changes to **Started**, pick the items that are composing the production's BOM. (The printout of the items that are involved in a production is called the picking list.) By default, the system suggests starting the quantity not yet started. Item and route consumption can also be picked in connection with **Start**.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: I checked current Microsoft Learn documentation for starting production orders and related production-control parameters. The docs confirm the Start action and that production orders can be started in batches/with quantity-related settings, but I couldn't find current official documentation that explicitly states the Start page still defaults the quantity to the amount 'not yet started.' Since Learn search/fetch did not provide direct evidence confirming or contradicting that exact default behavior, this claim can't be verified from the available official sources.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: Reporting a production order as finished makes the reported items available in inventory and frees resources for other production tasks.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
## Report production orders as finished

Use the **Report as finished** page to report all or a part of a production as finished. When you report an order as finished, it receives the status of **Report as finished**.

This process allows for the items that are reported as finished to be available in inventory and frees resources to schedule other production tasks. The report automatically sends information about the quantity of items produced, the number of units in error, and the cause of the errors.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Current Microsoft Learn documentation supports the main claim. The "Report production orders as finished" article says that when finished goods are reported as finished on a production order, they are "updated as on-hand in the inventory." The "Production process overview" also says the finished-goods quantity is updated in inventory at the "Reported as finished" stage. While the docs phrase the resource effect through production completion/status progression rather than the exact words "frees resources," that workflow is consistent with moving completed work off the order so capacity can be used for subsequent scheduling. No contradiction or retirement was found.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: If a production has not gone through prior lifecycle update steps, reporting it as finished triggers automatic updates that can include Estimation, Scheduling, Release, and Start.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
If a production has not been through the update steps in the production life cycle, Supply Chain Management does an automatic update. These updates can include the following steps in the life cycle:

- Estimation
- Scheduling
- Release
- Start
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Current Microsoft Learn documentation confirms the production life-cycle stages (Estimated, Scheduled, Released, Started, Reported as finished) and explains reporting as finished, but I could not find current official documentation explicitly stating that reporting a production order as finished automatically backfills missing prior steps such as Estimation, Scheduling, Release, and Start. The task docs instead describe reporting as finished from a production order already in Started status. Because the available Learn sources do not clearly verify or directly contradict the automatic-update behavior in the claim, this is inconclusive.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: Ending a production order generates a receipt transaction with Purchased status for the production item and deletes earlier receipt transactions that were generated.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
## End production orders

The final step in the life cycle of a production order is End. When production is complete and orders are formally ended, they are also cost-accounted. A receipt transaction with the **Purchased** status is generated for the production item. This transaction covers receipts for items that were created and have the status of **Ordered**, items that were reported-as-finished and have the status of **Received**, and receipt transactions that were generated earlier are deleted.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation confirms that ending a production order calculates actual costs, reverses estimated costs, and changes the order status to Ended, while reporting as finished is the step associated with the product receipt. I couldn't find current Microsoft Learn documentation that specifically verifies or contradicts the more detailed statement that ending generates a receipt transaction with Purchased status and deletes earlier receipt transactions, so this claim can't be conclusively grounded from the available official docs.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: When a production is ended, previously posted items and work in process are automatically reversed in the ledger, all journals are posted and closed, and actual costs are calculated from realized material and time consumption.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt: Previously posted items and work in process (WIP) are automatically reversed in the ledger and all journals are posted and closed. Actual costs are calculated when a production is ended. These costs are based on realized material and time consumption. You can compare actual costs to estimated material and time consumption costs that were calculated when the production order was estimated.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Current Microsoft Learn documentation supports the substance of this claim. The official production posting docs state that before a production order is ended, actual costs are calculated, all estimated material/labor/overhead costs are reversed and replaced with actual costs, physical transactions are reversed and financially updated at ending, and WIP accounts are settled when the production order is ended. Microsoft Learn also describes end-journal posting at this stage. While the docs do not use the exact phrase "all journals are posted and closed," the overall end-of-production behavior described in the claim matches current documentation.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: For finished items in final price calculation, ending production updates the original inventory transaction to Purchased status from Ordered or Received.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt:
- **Finished items** - The cost amount for finished items is calculated as **Number of finished items * Item's cost price = Realized cost amount**.

The item's cost price is taken from the item when you calculate costing. During the costing of item gains, the original inventory transaction is updated to the **Purchased** status from **Ordered** or **Received**.
- **Consumption of operations** - (Reported time consumption * Reported hourly cost price) + (Reported processed quantity *Reported quantity cost price) = Realized cost amount.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation supports the substance of this claim. The "Physical and financial updates" article states that reporting a production order as finished is a physical increase with status **Received**, and **production order costing** is a financial increase with status **Purchased**. The "Production postings" article also says that when a production order is ended, the physical transactions are reversed and the related inventory transactions are financially updated. Together, that backs the claim that finished-item transactions move from a physical state such as Received to a financial state Purchased during production costing/end processing.

module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.claim: When a production order reaches Ended status, it can no longer be updated.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.excerpt: When the production order is assigned the **Ended** status and can no longer be updated, the production order is cost accounted, and a receipt transaction with the **Purchased** status is generated for the produced item. All journals that are associated with the production order are closed.
module-2774acd7fd2536018da15f30b5e6ee2f1.reasoning: Microsoft Learn documentation supports the claim’s main point. The production process overview states that when a production order status changes to **Ended**, it “prevents any additional costs from being posted to a completed production order.” A related troubleshooting article also says raw material consumption can be adjusted only until the order reaches **Ended** status, implying updates stop at that point. This matches the learning content at a practical level.

Microsoft Entra ID supports two types of permissions: delegated permissions and application permissions.

* **Delegated permissions** are used by apps that have a signed-in user present. For these apps, either the user or an administrator consents to the permissions that the app requests. ## How scale works

When you scale an App Service plan, the needed infrastructure is added automatically. There's a time delay to scale operations while the infrastructure is being added. If you do several scale operations in sequence, the first infrastructure scale request is acted on and the others are queued. When the first scale operation finishes, the other infrastructure requests all operate together. And when the infrastructure is added, the App Service plans are assigned as appropriate. Creating a new App Service plan is itself a scale operation because it requests additional hardware. A scale operation usually takes 30-60 minutes to complete.

module-5f044d345476e3807d194c9d436a9a4e2.claim: Azure services that support availability zones are categorized as zonal services, zone-redundant services, or non-regional services.
module-5f044d345476e3807d194c9d436a9a4e2.excerpt:
Azure services that support availability zones fall into three categories:

 -  Zonal services: You pin the resource to a specific zone (for example, VMs, managed disks, IP addresses).
 -  Zone-redundant services: The platform replicates automatically across zones (for example, zone-redundant storage, SQL Database).
 -  Non-regional services: Services are always available from Azure geographies and are resilient to zone-wide outages as well as region-wide outages.

module-5f044d345476e3807d194c9d436a9a4e2.excerpt:
### Region pairs

Most Azure regions are paired with another region within the same geography (such as US, Europe, or Asia) at least 300 miles away. This approach allows for the replication of resources across a geography that helps reduce the likelihood of interruptions because of events such as natural disasters, civil unrest, power outages, or physical network outages that affect an entire region. For example, if a region in a pair was affected by a natural disaster, services would automatically fail over to the other region in its region pair.

Current docs say Microsoft associates some Azure regions into region pairs that are usually in the same geography, and that many newer regions are nonpaired; this aligns with the claim's use of "most" rather than "all." Learn also states paired regions are typically separated by at least 300 miles, with documented exceptions such as Brazil South being outside the same geography.

All license checks occur at the document line level. One document can contain lines that reference multiple licenses. When the system evaluates a license, it uses the same evaluation that it uses for restriction/exception rules. Ignoring fields that don't have a value, the evaluation considers any field that has a value in the license definition.

The same page also explains that even when a license is provided at the document level, it is assumed onto all lines and evaluation is still performed against the line being processed.
